row.team_price_text: Starter: from $299/mo billed annually (2,000 assets, unlimited user seats)
row.evidence: Lansweeper's pricing page lists Single sign-on (SSO) from the Starter plan, and its docs say "Lansweeper supports SAML and OIDC connections"; accounts are added by invitation and no SCIM endpoint is documented.
row.notes: New row. Asset-priced with unlimited user seats: Free (up to 100 assets), Starter from $299/mo and Pro from $528/mo billed annually, Enterprise custom; per-user fields stay null. SAML/OIDC SSO is on Starter and up. SSO creates or links a Lansweeper account by email, but site access comes from invitations (Site settings > Account management), so there is no SCIM and no IdP-driven deprovisioning. Okta and Entra setups use custom (non-catalogue) SAML apps. The Data API (inventory and audit trail) is POC-only on Starter/Pro, full on Enterprise; it does not manage site accounts. 'None' is by absence (rule 5).

plans.name: Starter
plans.price_text: From $299 per month, billed annually (2,000 assets)
plans.notes: Flat asset-based price; unlimited user seats. API limited to POC.

plans.name: Pro
plans.price_text: From $528 per month, billed annually (2,000 assets)

scim.notes: No SCIM in the docs index (llms.txt lists SSO, MFA, account invites, roles and groups only), the pricing comparison or the developer portal. 'false' is by absence (rule 5).

audit_log_api.notes: Audit trail retrievable via the Data API; the pricing page limits API access to POC on Starter and Pro.

user_api.notes: The Lansweeper Data API (GraphQL/REST, API key) exposes inventory data (assets, software, discovered users) and audit-trail data; no endpoint to manage Lansweeper site accounts, roles or invites is documented. Full API access is Enterprise; Starter/Pro limited to POC.

okta.notes: No OIN result; vendor guide configures a custom SAML app.

entra.notes: Vendor guide uses a non-gallery app; no Lansweeper tutorial in Microsoft's SaaS app tutorial index.

fallbacks.notes: SSO login creates or links a Lansweeper account by email, but site access still needs an invitation, so this is not JIT site provisioning.
